Paragraph Grouping for Screen Text

Screen text differs from scanned pages: fonts are crisp,
lines are short, and layouts mix menus with prose.
We group detected lines by their left edges and gaps.

Lines whose vertical gap is below 0.6 of the line height
and whose left edges align are merged into one paragraph.

A first-line indent, a sudden change of spacing, or a
different font size starts a new paragraph instead.

Chinese and Japanese lines are joined directly, while
Latin lines get a space and lose trailing hyphens.
